significance: Urbain Grandier, parish priest of Saint-Pierre du Marché at Loudun, was burned at the stake on 18 August 1634, convicted of bewitching the Ursuline nuns. His execution is the culmination of France's best-documented possession case and the central case study in the political instrumentalization of witch prosecution — Grandier had opposed Cardinal Richelieu and was prosecuted by a royal commission headed by Richelieu's cousin.
source_method: Archives Départementales de la Vienne; de Certeau, La Possession de Loudun (1970/2000); Levack, The Witch-Hunt in Early Modern Europe (2006)
